Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1565) Oct 14, 2026

  • The Edit Ref on screen follows the cut. In 1.0 (1557) and (1561) the Edit Ref drawn beside the conform was the conform's own frame number plus the Line up offset, so going from shot to shot showed parts of it out of order (frame grabs and the Record TC were right). It is now drawn at the frame of the cut the conform is showing, and runs on through a freeze.
  • Line Up by Picture. An Edit Ref with black or a slate before the cut, and no timecode to say so, no longer has to be lined up by eye: Line Up by Picture finds the offset from where its cuts fall against the cut's, checks a frame of up to ten shots, and offers it (Apply +7). Nothing moves until you apply it.
  • Trim Handles on a conformed clip. A clip of a conformed cut plays only the frames the cut uses. Trim Handles used to widen it to the whole camera file, and the Edit Ref beside it stopped following; it now leaves the clip alone, and a session saved that way plays the clip's own frames again.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1476) Oct 12, 2026

  • DPX sequences play. 8, 10, 12 and 16-bit DPX files open and play like any other image sequence, read as the color space set for DPX in Settings, Color.
  • A tall floating Playlist with thumbnails could stop the app. Fixed.
  • Small fixes.

1.0 (build 1441) Oct 11, 2026

  • Network is in the Review menu. Review ▸ Network; it was under Window. It is also in the right-click Review menu.
  • A playlist on a network drive no longer slows the window. Whether each clip's file is there is checked in the background.
  • Locate Media… reads a folder in the background. A line above the toolbar says how far it has got.

Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1561) Oct 14, 2026

  • Camera originals from a drive of shoot days. Camera Folders… has an Only in folders named field: choose the drive and type Camera Raw, and the transcodes beside each day's camera raw are left out of the search. A camera clip recorded as QuickTime and a transcode of the same name and timecode are no longer taken one for the other: the clip says Check.

Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1557) Oct 14, 2026

  • The Edit Ref beside the conform. Choose the editor's movie of the cut (an MP4 or QuickTime) in the Conform window, or drop it there, and Compare Edit Ref (⌥⌘B) shows it beside the conform. It follows the cut from clip to clip, on the frame of the cut the conform is showing, so a wrong join or a slipped shot shows at a glance. It lines up by its timecode, or with the cut's first frame when it has none; Line up moves it a frame at a time. It is read as Rec.709 (or whatever you set on its side of the compare), kept with the session (choosing it or lining it up asks to be saved), and never sent to a review room.
  • The row the playhead is on. In the Conform window the row playing has a bar at its edge and a tint of its own, and keeps them when you click another row. The header says which shot of how many is playing, and the list no longer scrolls from under the pointer.
  • Retimes past 400% play to time. A conformed clip faster than 400% or slower than 5% plays in the time the cut gives it, as an edit application plays it.
  • A joined piece keeps its own ramp. When one of the events joined into a shot has a speed ramp of its own, its keys stay in the shot's speed line, so the plate's frame map has the right frame for every frame of the cut.
  • Open from Link no longer quits Asobi. A link that isn't a review is downloaded and opened as media; when the download ended, Asobi quit instead. A link that opens a web page (a share page, a sign-in) now says so, rather than opening nothing.
